description:
=== DONE (s473t5e) ===

FOUND s473t5e (#1501 round 6, `re/` CHECK 2) as t/re/charset.t's ONE fact.
That file's every assertion is of the form

    my $a = "0"; $a =~ qr/ (?a: [_[:digit:]] ) /x;
    ... "0" is a [:digit:] under /a

and all 501 of its blessed fail rows (plus 2,776 rows short) read
`ok -> not ok` for that shape.

`docs/not-supported.md` "Regex encoding modifiers (/a, /d, /l, /u)" blesses
IGNORING the modifiers -- cl-ppcre always matches with /u semantics -- and it
said they were "accepted in the source but silently ignored".  That was FALSE
of the INLINE spelling: `a` `aa` `d` `l` `u` are not cl-ppcre flags, and
cl-ppcre does not ignore an unknown flag, it rejects the pattern:

    Regex syntax error: Character 'a' may not follow '(?'.
        at position 2 in string "(?a:\\d)"

So the match answered 0 where perl says 1, with a warning on stderr.  The
trailing spelling `/a` really was ignored, which is why the entry read as
true.

FIX: `%pcl-strip-charset-flags`, one more pass in `perl-regex-to-ppcre`'s
chain (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), two lines below the `(?^` -> `(?` rewrite it is
modelled on -- the same mechanism, a flag cl-ppcre does not know removed so
the pattern compiles.  It touches ONLY a run made entirely of perl's modifier
letters followed by `:` or `)`:

    (?a:X)   -> (?:X)        (?ai:X)  -> (?i:X)
    (?aa:X)  -> (?:X)        (?a-i:X) -> (?-i:X)
    (?u:X) (?l:X) (?d:X)     (?a)     -> nothing at all
    (?:  (?=  (?!  (?>  (?#  (?<n>  (?<=  (?<!  (?&  (?(1)  (?{   untouched

THE BREAKING CASE, probed and guarded: `/\(?u:/` is an optional LITERAL paren
followed by `u:`, not a modifier group, and rewriting it would silently drop
the `u`.  A `(?<!\\)` lookbehind keeps an escaped paren out of the pass.  The
price is that a DOUBLED backslash before a real group declines, which leaves
cl-ppcre to reject that pattern in its own words exactly as it does today --
loud, not wrong.  (The same exposure exists in the two sibling passes, `(?^`
and the POSIX one; this is not a new class.)

PROBED (scratch/s473t5e/probe-charset2.pl): 29 cases -- every charset letter,
the combined and negated flag forms, all eight other `(?` forms, the
escaped-paren pair and a literal `[(?a:]` class.  27 byte-identical to perl
5.40.3.  The two that differ are the ruled ones:
  * `\(?d)` is INVALID perl (unmatched paren) -- design principle 9; PCL
    declines loudly, which is how the lookbehind guard shows itself working;
  * `"\x{100}" =~ /(?a:\w)/` is 1 in PCL and 0 in perl -- that IS the blessed
    entry: the SEMANTICS stay ignored.  The entry now says so in those words.

GUARD: `Pl/t/regex-extended-mode-01.t` rows 7 + 8 (6 -> 8 rows; that file
already owns inline mode-modifier groups), both FAILING on a `git archive
ee53ce76` extraction.  Runtime-only, so emission cannot move and there is no
generation bump.

MEASURED: see the s473t5e session-log section for t/re/charset.t's verdict
before and after.
